He played [[college basketball]] for three seasons with the [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]], then transferred to [[Howard University]] before ultimately opting out of the season, then entered the [[2021 NBA draft]], but was not selected. ==Early life== Eastern's first name, Nojel, is an [[ananym]] of his father's name, Lejon. He was raised by his mother, Tamala Reed, who worked for the [[Chicago Transit Authority]]. Eastern had [[attention deficit hyperactivity disorder]] since his youth. Even though his mother worked in Chicago, he attended school in [[Evanston, Illinois]] due to the district's superior academics. From fourth to eighth grade, Eastern lived with Travis Ransom, a family friend.{{cite web |last1=Cardi |first1=Julia |title=Chasing Nojel |url=https://news.medill.northwestern.edu/chicago/chasing-nojel/ |website=Medill Reports |publisher=[[Northwestern University]] |accessdate=May 17, 2020 |date=July 13, 2016}} ==High school career== Eastern played four years of [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball for [[Evanston Township High School]] in Evanston. As a sophomore, he averaged 15.7 points, 5.3 rebounds and three assists per game, leading his team to the [[Central Suburban League]] South championship and a Class 4A regional title.{{cite web |last1=Harness |first1=Matt |title=Evanston's Nojel Eastern makes All-Area Boys Basketball Second Team |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/evanston/sports/ct-bcr-nojel-eastern-evanston-tl-0402-20150331-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=May 17, 2020 |date=March 31, 2015}} In April 2015, Eastern dislocated his left ankle and fractured two bones in it during an [[Amateur Athletic Union]] game, before undergoing surgery.{{cite web |last1=Harness |first1=Matt |title=Coaches don't think injury will affect recruitment of Nojel Eastern |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/evanston/sports/ct-evr-nojel-eastern-ankle-injury-recruiting-tl-0507-20150505-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=May 17, 2020 |date=May 5, 2015}} In his junior season, he averaged 14.9 points, 6.5 rebounds and four assists per game, helping Evanston Township win Central Suburban South and Class 4A regional titles.{{cite web |last1=Mahoney |first1=Dennis |title=Eastern's clutch play lifts Wildkits to regional title |url=https://evanstonnow.com/story/sports/dennis-mahoney/2016-03-05/74709/easterns-clutch-play-lifts-wildkits-to-regional-title |website=Evanston Now |accessdate=May 17, 2020 |date=March 5, 2016}} As a senior, Eastern averaged 15.6 points, 7.1 rebounds and 4.2 assists per game and was named [[Pioneer Press]] All-Area Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Shalin |first1=Dan |title=All-Area Boys Basketball First Team: Nojel Eastern, Evanston |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/evanston/sports/ct-evr-nojel-eastern-basketball-first-team-tl-0330-20170329-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=May 17, 2020 |date=March 29, 2017}} He was the runner-up to [[Mark Smith (basketball)|Mark Smith]] for the [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] award.{{cite web |last1=Larkin |first1=Will |title=Edwardsville's Mark Smith named Mr. Basketball; Rock Island's Brea Beal is Ms. Basketball |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/high-school/ct-edwardsville-s-mark-smith-named-mr-basketball-rock-island-brea-beal-is-ms-basketball-20170321-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=May 17, 2020 |date=March 21, 2017}} ===Recruiting=== On November 16, 2016, Eastern committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] over offers from [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] and [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], among others. He was drawn to Purdue because of its coaching staff and its proximity.{{cite web |last1=Narang |first1=Bob |title=Nojel Eastern picks Purdue because of coaches, proximity to home |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/evanston/sports/ct-evr-nojel-eastern-purdue-basketball-evantson-tl-1116-20161116-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=May 17, 2020 |date=November 16, 2016}} Eastern was considered a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by major recruiting services.{{cite web |title=Nojel Eastern |url=https://purduesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/nojel-eastern/8368 |publisher=Purdue University Athletics |accessdate=May 17, 2020}} {{College athlete recruit career== [[File:Brandon Johns Nojel Eastern.jpg|thumb|right|Eastern defended by Brandon Johns Jr. of [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] in February 2020]] As a freshman at Purdue, Eastern averaged 2.9 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game in the role of a defensive specialist off the bench.{{cite web |last1=Baird |first1=Nathan |title=As Nojel Eastern continues to prove himself, Purdue basketball's potential rises |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2018/11/17/purdue-basketballs-nojel-eastern-making-palpable-early-impact/2039055002/ |website=[[Journal & Courier]] |accessdate=June 2, 2020 |date=November 17, 2018}} After the season, he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] without hiring an agent, before withdrawing from the draft.{{cite web |last1=Osipoff |first1=Michael |title=Evanston grad Nojel Eastern 'living in the moment' at Purdue after NBA draft process |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/post-tribune/sports/ct-evr-nojel-eastern-evanston-purdue-nba-draft-tl-0719-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=June 2, 2020 |date=July 14, 2018}} On March 9, 2019, Eastern scored a career-high 15 points in a 70–57 win over [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]].{{cite news |title=Edwards scores 21, No. 11 Purdue beats Northwestern 70–57 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082546 |accessdate=June 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 9, 2019}} In his sophomore season, he became a regular starter and averaged 7.5 points, a team-high 5.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.1 steals per game, earning [[Big Ten Conference]] All-Defensive honors. Eastern became the first Purdue point guard to lead the team in rebounding since at least 1954.{{cite web |last1=Baird |first1=Nathan |title=Purdue's unconventional, invaluable Nojel Eastern returns home with championship at stake |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2019/03/07/purdues-unconventional-invaluable-nojel-eastern-returns-northwesten/3090981002/ |website=[[Journal & Courier]] |accessdate=June 2, 2020 |date=March 7, 2019}} By the time he was a junior, he became Purdue's top defender, with the ability to guard all five positions.{{cite web |last1=Glaspie |first1=Akeem |title=Nojel Eastern's winning plays are contagious for Purdue basketball |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/purdue/2020/01/03/purdue-mens-basketball-nojel-easterns-defense-closes-out-double-ot-win-minnesota-golden-gophers/2803968001/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |accessdate=June 2, 2020 |date=January 3, 2020}} As a junior, Eastern averaged 4.9 points, four rebounds and 2.7 assists per game, earning Big Ten All-Defensive accolades for a second time. He led his team in assists and steals. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Carmin |first1=Mike |title=Purdue basketball's Nojel Eastern submits name in NBA Draft |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2020/04/26/purdue-basketballs-nojel-eastern-submits-name-nba-draft/3031112001/ |website=[[Journal & Courier]] |accessdate=June 2, 2020 |date=April 26, 2020}} On May 12, 2020, Eastern announced that he would transfer from Purdue.{{cite magazine |last1=Douglas |first1=Brett |title=Breaking News: Nojel Eastern Enters Transfer Portal |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/basketball/purdue-nojel-eastern-enters-transfer-portal |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=June 2, 2020 |date=May 12, 2020}} Two days later, he committed to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] for his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Purdue transfer Nojel Eastern headed to Michigan |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29175428/purdue-transfer-nojel-eastern-headed-michigan |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=June 2, 2020 |date=May 14, 2020}} However, on June 17, Eastern announced that he would not play for Michigan after he was unable to clear the admission to the school.{{cite web |last1=Cobb |first1=David |title=Purdue transfer Nojel Eastern no longer heading to Michigan after being denied admission |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/purdue-transfer-nojel-eastern-no-longer-heading-to-michigan-after-being-denied-admission/ |work=CBS Sports |accessdate=June 17, 2020 |date=June 17, 2020}} On August 6, 2020, Eastern committed to continue his career at [[Howard Bison men's basketball|Howard]].{{cite web |title=Nojel Eastern, a P5 transfer, lands at Howard |url=https://hbcugameday.com/2020/08/06/nojel-eastern-a-p5-transfer-lands-at-howard/ |website=HBCU Gameday |accessdate=August 6, 2020 |date=August 6, 2020}} Before playing a game, he quit the team on January 3, 2021, to pursue a professional career and train for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Nojel Eastern, who nearly transferred to Michigan, opting out of season with Howard |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2021/01/03/nojel-eastern-michigan-wolverines-opting-out-season-howard/4122640001/ |access-date=January 27, 2021 |work=[[Detroit News]] |date=January 3, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Rayos de Hermosillo (2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Eastern joined the [[Long Island Nets]] for training camp after a successful tryout.{{cite web|title=No big surprises on Long Island Nets training camp roster|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2021/10/25/22745627/no-big-surprises-on-long-island-nets-training-camp-roster|website=NetsDaily.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 7, 2021}} However, he was waived on October 27, 2021.{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Waive Nojel Eastern|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/long-island-nets-waive-nojel-eastern/n-5758674|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 27, 2021|access-date=November 7, 2021}} On March 10, 2023, Eastern debuted with the [[Rayos de Hermosillo]] of the [[Circuito de Baloncesto de la Costa del Pacífico]] (CIBACOPA). He earned All-Star honors.{{cite news|first=Marcos|last=Romero|title=Lucen talentos en Juego de Estrellas Cibacopa 2023|url=https://www.elsoldetijuana.com.mx/deportes/lucen-talentos-en-juego-de-estrellas-cibacopa-2023-9961504.html|work=El Sol de Tijuana|date=April 23, 2023|access-date=June 4, 2023|language=es}} ===Halcones Rojos Veracruz (2023)=== On August 4, 2023, Eastern signed with [[Halcones Rojos Veracruz]] from the Mexican [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional|LNBP]].{{cite news|title=Nojel Eastern jugará con Halcones Rojos en la LNBP|url=https://www.masnoticias.mx/nojel-eastern-jugara-con-halcones-rojos-en-la-lnbp/|website=MasNoticias.mx|date=August 4, 2023|access-date=December 8, 2023|language=es}} ===Iowa Wolves (2023–present)=== On October 29, 2023, Eastern was picked 41st overall in the [[2023 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite web|title=2023 NBA G League Draft|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2023-nba-g-league-draft|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} In a 125-120 victory over the [[Stockton Kings]] on February 8, 2025, he scored a career-high 34 points. In the 2024-25 season, Eastern averaged 12.9 points, 2.9 assists, 5.4 rebounds and 1.4 steals per game. He was signed by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on September 17.{{cite web |title=Timberwolves Sign Guard Nojel Eastern |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-guard-nojel-eastern |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 28, 2025 |date=September 17, 2025}} Eastern was waived the following day.{{cite web |title=Timberwolves Sign, Waive Nojel Eastern |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/09/timberwolves-sign-nojel-eastern.html |website=HoopsRumors |access-date=September 28, 2025 |date=September 18, 2025}} On November 6, 2025, Eastern was named to the [[Iowa Wolves]] opening night roster.{{cite web|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/iowa-wolves-announce-opening-night-roster|title=Iowa Wolves Announce Opening Night Roster|website=gleague.nba.com|date=November 6, 2025|access-date=November 6, 2025}} ==National team career== Eastern and his Purdue teammates represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] at the [[Basketball at the 2017 Summer Universiade|2017 Summer Universiade]] in [[Taipei]]. He averaged 5.6 points, 2.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 14.5 minutes per game, helping his team win the silver medal.{{cite web |last1=Jacobson |first1=Jake |title=Purdue Men's Basketball: International tournament reinforces veteran experience |url=https://www.purdueexponent.org/sports/article_277cfdfb-0d64-535e-942f-8832c5135063.html |website=[[Purdue Exponent]] |accessdate=June 1, 2020 |date=October 2, 2017}}{{cite web |title=Getting to Know: Nojel Eastern |url=https://purduesports.com/news/2017/10/9/Getting_to_Know_Nojel_Eastern.aspx |publisher=Purdue University Athletics
